metaTitle: tailwind-dictionary — a Tailwind CSS theme from design tokens
metaDescription: An npm package that builds a Tailwind CSS 4 or 3 theme from Figma, Tokens Studio or Style Dictionary JSON tokens: light, dark and any other themes with one command, no build scripts.

hero.titleStart: A Tailwind theme from design tokens,
hero.description: tailwind-dictionary turns JSON tokens from Figma, Tokens Studio or Style Dictionary into a Tailwind CSS 4 or 3 theme — with light, dark and any other themes. One config.json instead of a build script.

cta.title: Try it yourself
cta.text: Paste your tokens into the playground — the theme builds right in the browser, nothing to install. Or install the package and run one command.

demo.title: What you get
demo.text: A palette and the light and dark theme colors in DTCG format — and the theme the package builds from them. This is real build output: switch the Tailwind version to compare.

why.title: Why a separate package
why.description: A Tailwind theme edited by hand drifts away from the design over time. If colors and sizes already live in tokens, build the theme from them.

accent.title: Always in sync with the design
accent.text: The designer updated a color in Figma, you exported the variables and ran one command. No hunting for where that color is written in CSS and no checking that nothing got lost.

dark.title: Why not Style Dictionary?
dark.text: Style Dictionary is a powerful tool, but you would have to describe the Tailwind theme format, @theme, semantic variables and theme switching yourself, in a JS script you also have to maintain. Here it is already done, covered by tests and configured with JSON.

items.title: A JSON config, no code
items.text: Token paths and their mapping to Tailwind theme keys live in one config.json. The JSON Schema suggests fields right in the editor.

items.title: Figma export as is
items.text: Export modes in Figma gives one file per mode — plug them in without conversion. Unitless numbers get px or rem.

items.title: DTCG and the legacy format
items.text: The W3C Design Tokens 2025.10 format with composite typography and shadow. Style Dictionary tokens with a value field work too.

items.title: Any number of themes
items.text: Light, dark, high-contrast or brand themes. They switch with a data-theme attribute on any element; light and dark follow the system setting.

items.title: Tailwind 4 and 3
items.text: For v4 — theme.css with @theme, for v3 — an object for tailwind.config.js. The tokens are the same for both versions.

items.title: Clear errors and watch mode
items.text: A broken token reference is one line with the token path and file name. In watch mode the theme rebuilds on every token change.

themes.title: Themes on any element
themes.description: The block below is built on the pbstyles theme that tailwind-dictionary generates. The switch changes only the data-theme attribute on the container — the classes stay the same.
themes.label: Block theme

card.title: Weekly report
card.text: Background, text, border and button colors come from the semantic tokens of the current theme.

steps.title: From Figma to code in four steps
steps.description: An example for Tailwind 4 and the native Figma variables export. For Tokens Studio and Style Dictionary, only the file paths change.

items.title: Export the variables
items.text: In Figma: Variables → right-click the collection → Export modes. You get a file with primitives and one file per mode.

items.title: Describe the config
items.text: Primitives go to source, modes go to themes. In themeAliases, specify which token groups map to which Tailwind theme keys.

items.title: Build the theme
items.text: Run npx tailwind-dictionary and import the result after Tailwind. The default Tailwind theme is replaced with your tokens.

items.title: Write regular classes
items.text: Classes are built from your tokens: bg-primary, rounded-12. In the dark theme, bg-primary becomes a different color on its own — no markup changes needed.

proof.title: In a real project
proof.text: The pbstyles theme is built with tailwind-dictionary — it is the foundation of the design system behind this site and its docs. The pbstyles config is public, so you can use it as a template.

fit.title: Who it is for
yes: your tokens already live in Figma, Tokens Studio or Style Dictionary
the project uses Tailwind CSS 4 or 3
you need light, dark or brand themes
the theme should be built from tokens, not edited by hand
no: there are no tokens and won't be — a few variables are easier to write in @theme by hand
the project doesn't use Tailwind — for CSS variables, LESS and SCSS there is mixin-dictionary
you need custom Style Dictionary transforms and formats — then your own build script is more convenient
